Worse, a concurrent run could also mark the reminder `scheduled: true` while another run is mid-failure, leading to inconsistent state. findings.title: deleteMany with retryCount > 1 deletes ALL workflow reminders across all methods, not just SMS
findings.body: The cleanup query at the top of the handler uses `OR: [{ method: SMS, scheduledDate <= now }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]`. The second OR branch has no `method` filter, so it deletes every WorkflowReminder row in the table with retryCount > 1 — including EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders. Email reminders are scheduled by a different cron job (scheduleEmailReminders) and may legitimately have retryCount > 1 (or the column may be incremented elsewhere), so this change can silently delete email/WhatsApp reminders that are still pending, causing missed notifications. The retryCount-based deletion should be scoped to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (e.g. nest it inside the first branch or add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to the second OR condition).

findings.title: Reminders with no message or no sendTo are never retried and never cleaned up, causing an infinite silent loop
findings.body: The retry increment only happens inside `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)` (the else branch when scheduleSMS returns falsy) or in the catch block. If `message` is null/empty (e.g. workflowStep has neither reminderBody nor template REMINDER) or `sendTo` is missing (no smsReminderNumber on the booking and action is SMS_ATTENDEE), the code falls through without updating the row: `scheduled` stays false and `retryCount` stays 0. The reminder is then re-fetched by the `findMany` on every cron run forever (it matches `scheduled: false` and `scheduledDate <= now + 7 days`), and the deleteMany cleanup never removes it because retryCount never exceeds 1 and — for future-dated reminders — scheduledDate is not past. This is a busy-loop / unbounded row growth issue. The code should either increment retryCount (or delete the reminder) when message/sendTo is missing, or log and skip explicitly.

findings.title: Read-modify-write of retryCount is not atomic; concurrent cron runs can lose increments
findings.body: The handler reads `retryCount` in the initial `findMany` (line 58), then later writes `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` (lines 184 and 195) based on the stale in-memory value. If two instances of this cron endpoint run concurrently (overlapping schedules, multiple pods, or a long-running invocation overlapping the next tick), both read the same retryCount and both write the same incremented value, so a failure is only counted once. Worse, a concurrent run could also mark the reminder `scheduled: true` while another run is mid-failure, leading to inconsistent state. Prisma's atomic `increment` should be used instead: `data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }`. The same non-atomic pattern means the `retryCount > 1` deletion threshold can be defeated by overlapping runs, letting permanently-failing reminders (e.g. invalid phone numbers) persist indefinitely — the exact problem this PR is trying to fix.

findings.title: Off-by-one: reminders are deleted when retryCount > 1, i.e. only after the third failure, not the second as described
findings.body: The PR description says 'after scheduling failed twice we delete the workflow reminder', but the cleanup condition is `retryCount: { gt: 1 }`, which only matches retryCount >= 2. A reminder starts at retryCount 0; the first failure sets it to 1 (still kept), the second failure sets it to 2 (deleted on the next cron run). So the reminder is actually attempted three times (initial attempt + 2 retries) before deletion, not twice. Either change the condition to `gte: 1` (delete after the second failure sets retryCount to 1... note this would delete after the first retry) or, to match 'failed twice' semantics with the current increment placement, use `gte: 2`/`gt: 1` and fix the description — but as written the code and description disagree, and the deletion happens one cron cycle later than the retryCount reaches 2, so a reminder with retryCount = 2 is retried once more before being deleted.

findings.title: A failure in the retryCount update inside the catch block is unhandled and aborts the whole cron run
findings.body: Inside the `catch (error)` block, the code awaits `prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` to increment retryCount. If that database update itself throws (transient DB error, connection issue), the exception propagates out of the catch block, out of the for-loop, and rejects the handler — the `res.status(200).json(...)` at line 201 is never reached and remaining reminders in `unscheduledReminders` are never processed. The same applies to the update in the else branch at line 179. A failure to record the retry should not prevent processing of other reminders; wrap the retryCount update in its own try/catch (or use a non-throwing update) so one bad row doesn't abort the batch.
